claims: The Artemis II mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew completed a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission involved flying around the Moon without landing on its surface.
The Orion spacecraft landed safely in the Pacific Ocean.
According to NASA officials, the Artemis II crew reached the farthest point from Earth (over 250,000 miles) any human has ever traveled.
NASA and U.S. Navy personnel successfully extracted the Artemis II crew from the capsule.
The Artemis II crew is reported to be in good health.
Artemis II was a crewed test flight to prepare for future moon landings.
Artemis III is planned to land on the Moon.
